---
title: "Sparse relation attention"
---

# Sparse relation attention

`cellerator::modeling::cuda::sparse_attention_fp16` and
`sparse_attention_fp32` implement scaled dot-product attention over an explicit
CSR relation. For query row `i`, only keys in
`key_ids[offsets[i]:offsets[i+1]]` participate. An empty row yields a zero
output. The scale is supplied by the caller; channel semantics and the meaning
of a relation remain model-owned.

The API takes query `[Q,D]`, key `[N,D]`, value `[N,V]`, and output `[Q,V]`
row-major buffers. It performs stable segmented softmax and accumulates in
FP32, including FP16 storage variants. Caller-owned `SparseAttentionWorkspace`
holds edge logits/probabilities and per-query backward reductions. No dense
adjacency, automatic mask, allocation, or stream synchronization is introduced.

The first-order VJP computes query, key, and value gradients into FP32 buffers.
`GradientWriteMode::zero` asynchronously clears buffers before applying the
gradient; `accumulate` adds into them. Repeated keys in different query rows
are reduced with FP32 atomics, so key/value gradient reduction order depends on
device scheduling. Backward consumes the probabilities written by a preceding
forward call and requires the same inputs, scale, and CSR plan; keep that
workspace unmodified and order the calls on the same stream or with an explicit
stream dependency. CSR indices are discrete and have no gradient here.

The caller must ensure monotone CSR offsets with `offsets[0] == 0` and
`offsets[Q] == edge_count`, in-range key IDs, non-overlapping workspace and
payload/gradient buffers, matching device residency, and sufficient capacities.
Plan data remains live until stream completion. These contracts are not checked
by copying device metadata back to the host. The current implementation is a
correctness-oriented baseline; compilation alone provides no performance or
runtime-correctness qualification.

`tests/framework/cuda/attention_smoke.cu` compares device results with an
independent reference. The V100 matrix checks staged and fused row lengths
across warp boundaries, backward behavior, and a large reduction case. The
[validation report](../planning/v100-framework-2026-10-29/REPORT.md) records
tested shapes, tolerances and sanitizer results. These correctness checks do
not measure a workload-level speedup.

## Optional fused small-row path

`sparse_attention_fused_small_fp16` and
`sparse_attention_fused_small_fp32` are explicit experimental entrypoints.
Rows with at most 32 edges keep scoring, softmax, and value aggregation within
one warp, avoiding a materialized logits round trip for those rows. They still
write edge probabilities for the existing backward API. Larger rows use the
staged path; the original forward entrypoints retain their existing behavior.

The design draws on KernelBender's producer/consumer ownership guidance in
`references/compositions/ownership-fragments.md`. Its focused V100 correctness
cases are recorded in the
[validation report](../planning/v100-framework-2026-10-29/REPORT.md). It remains
an alternative without a measured speedup or automatic selection.
Compare the complete forward/backward path, including workspace and preparation
costs, before choosing it for a workload.
